headline: High-risk shared filesystem and write-capable pair create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while unstructured reads files and writes outputs in a separate document-processing flow. Because Cline’s shared state is via filesystem and unstructured can process documents from files, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary through files even without a direct channel. This is plausible in default workspace/document pipelines, though not proven to be raw instruction parsing.
conditions: IF Cline ingests unstructured-produced files as instructions or tool context
IF both agents operate on the same workspace or document directory
IF unstructured outputs attacker-controlled text that Cline later reads
mitigations: Separate input and output directories for the two agents
Disable automatic ingestion of generated documents into Cline
Add a manual review step before Cline consumes unstructured outputs
Use file naming conventions that prevent accidental pickup
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and has broad network egress; unstructured processes documents, images, and text. If they share a workspace, sensitive files can move from Cline into unstructured’s document pipeline or vice versa. The profiles do not show encryption or access controls, so leakage is plausible in default shared-folder setups, but not enough for high because no uncontrolled third-party upload is explicit for both.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same filesystem path
IF source code or screenshots are placed into unstructured’s document inputs
IF unstructured outputs are stored where Cline can read them
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers
Mount only read-only inputs into unstructured
Keep screenshots and secrets out of shared folders
Restrict Cline’s workspace to non-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Cline also modifies git state and runs in a per-workspace session with shared state via filesystem. That creates a direct conflict on the same mutable workspace, and concurrent edits can corrupt files or git history. The profiles do not mention locking, so uncertainty pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF Cline modifies git state while unstructured writes generated artifacts
IF no external lock or serialization is configured
mitigations: Assign disjoint working directories
Pause one agent while the other writes
Commit or snapshot before handoff
Avoid concurrent git operations
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can produce browser-derived outputs and code changes, while unstructured can transform documents and text. If unstructured treats Cline’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream document extraction or file generation. There is no explicit verification or critique step in either profile, but no direct action authority like email or deployment is shown, so medium fits.
conditions: IF unstructured consumes Cline-generated text without validation
IF Cline’s browser-derived content is used as source material for unstructured
IF downstream artifacts are published or reused automatically
mitigations: Require human review of Cline outputs before ingestion
Validate extracted facts against original sources
Keep generated artifacts separate from source documents
Add checksum checks between stages
requires-engineering: implement schema validation

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots, while unstructured processes documents, images, and text with allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: sensitive screenshots or documents could be routed through different retention regimes if the same data class is shared. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of the same content.
conditions: IF regulated documents or screenshots are processed by both agents
IF retention or logging policies differ between the two services
IF the same sensitive data class is exported from Cline into unstructured
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to either agent
Review retention settings for both tools
Use redacted test documents
Keep API keys out of shared workspaces
requires-engineering: document a data-handling policy
